introduction.text: Puerto Galera brings together coastal livelihoods, forest habitats and a long relationship with the sea. Its cultural story also includes the living nito-weaving tradition of Iraya-Mangyan artisans in Talipanan.

collectibles.name: Nito basket token
collectibles.designNotes: Proposed artisan-approved design; replace the generic shell pickup.

collectibles.name: Boat postcard
collectibles.designNotes: Symbolic livelihood token, not an antique or wildlife specimen.

discoveries.title: A biosphere landscape
discoveries.text: UNESCO records Puerto Galera as a biosphere reserve nominated in 1977.

discoveries.title: Beyond the beach
discoveries.text: The reserve includes forests, mangroves and coral reefs as well as coastal ecosystems.

discoveries.title: Living craft
discoveries.text: Iraya-Mangyan artisans in Talipanan make functional nito baskets, trays and other woven objects.

discoveries.title: Learning across generations
discoveries.text: Ayala Foundation's account describes artisans learning weaving from family members.

discoveries.title: Sea and livelihood
discoveries.text: UNESCO identifies fishing and subsistence farming as earlier income sources, alongside later tourism work.

visitorChallenge.text: Enjoy reefs without touching coral or chasing wildlife. Leave shells in their habitat and support locally made alternatives.
visitorChallenge.note: General conservation guidance adapted to a game; not asserted as a municipal ordinance.

recap.question: Which material is associated with the documented Iraya-Mangyan craft here?
recap.onIncorrect: Explain the linked discovery and allow retry. Keep run rewards.
recap.reward: Optional journal reflection badge; never gate core travel progress.

journal.title: Weaving and the sea
journal.text: A basket can represent skilled work, while a reef represents a living habitat. Discover both without turning wildlife or community traditions into things to take.
journal.note: Draft editorial synthesis; factual basis is in linked discovery records.

introduction.text: San Teodoro combines waterfalls and other nature destinations with a history linked to Subaan. Coconut-based enterprise provides a documented connection between everyday work and the town's adventure theme.

collectibles.name: Coconut-product parcel

collectibles.name: Waterfall photo token
collectibles.designNotes: Observe the river landscape rather than collect live fish.

discoveries.title: Earlier name
discoveries.text: The provincial history identifies Subaan as San Teodoro's earlier name.

discoveries.title: An earlier center
discoveries.text: The same history places the old town center in present-day Lumangbayan.

discoveries.title: Coconut enterprise
discoveries.text: A provincial project report identifies a San Teodoro enterprise producing coconut-based goods.

discoveries.title: Aras Falls
discoveries.text: Aras Falls is listed among San Teodoro's freshwater attractions.

discoveries.title: Botolan Falls
discoveries.text: Botolan Falls is another waterfall listed for San Teodoro.

visitorChallenge.text: Bring a refillable bottle and carry packaging away from streams. Follow the guidance of local site caretakers.

journal.text: This page joins the Subaan history with waterfall observation and coconut enterprise. A place can hold several identities beyond the scenery in a single photograph.

introduction.text: Baco is associated with Mount Halcon and river landscapes. Its histories also name Iraya and Alangan communities, reminding visitors that the mountain setting is a lived cultural landscape.

collectibles.name: Mountain postcard
collectibles.designNotes: Replace the generic steep souvenir with Halcon's reference-led broad ridge.

collectibles.name: Paco fern illustration
collectibles.designNotes: Optional story token only; name-origin account is oral, not proven etymology.

discoveries.title: Mountain identity
discoveries.text: The provincial tourism listing locates Mount Halcon in Baco.

discoveries.title: Water landscapes
discoveries.text: Baco's history lists rivers, rapids and waterfalls among its landscape features.

discoveries.title: Distinct communities
discoveries.text: The history names Iraya and Alangan communities in Baco; these are not interchangeable identities.

discoveries.title: One name account
discoveries.text: One local account links Baco's name with paco, an edible fern.

discoveries.title: Another name account
discoveries.text: A different account connects the name with uneven, flood-affected roads.

visitorChallenge.text: Use permitted paths, respect closures and leave wild plants where they grow. Listen to local guides and community hosts.
visitorChallenge.note: Proposed respectful-behavior mechanic; not quoted local rules. Have site custodians review.

recap.question: Which mountain is associated with Baco in the tourism listing?
recap.onIncorrect: Explain the linked discovery and allow retry. Keep run rewards.
recap.reward: Optional journal reflection badge; never gate core travel progress.

journal.title: A mountain and many voices
journal.text: The Halcon landscape and Baco's communities deserve careful listening. Keep alternative name stories labeled as accounts, and let community contributors explain their own heritage.
journal.note: Draft editorial synthesis; factual basis is in linked discovery records.

introduction.text: Calapan City is Oriental Mindoro's capital and commercial center. Its heritage destinations and coastal conservation areas offer stories of city life, cultural learning and care for nearby habitats.

collectibles.name: Heritage museum ticket

collectibles.name: Mangrove observation badge
collectibles.designNotes: Observe plants; do not collect seedlings from the wild.

discoveries.title: Provincial center
discoveries.text: Calapan is identified as the provincial capital and a commercial center.

discoveries.title: Cityhood
discoveries.text: Calapan's cityhood was ratified through a plebiscite on 21 March 1998.

discoveries.title: Museum discovery
discoveries.text: The provincial tourism directory lists the Oriental Mindoro Heritage Museum in Calapan.

discoveries.title: Silonay
discoveries.text: DENR's monitoring record identifies Silonay Mangrove Conservation Area among Calapan's coastal sites.

discoveries.title: Harka Piloto
discoveries.text: The same DENR record identifies Harka Piloto as a fish sanctuary.

visitorChallenge.text: Observe mangroves and sanctuary wildlife without disturbing them. Keep boardwalks and coastal spaces free of litter.
visitorChallenge.note: Proposed respectful-behavior mechanic; not quoted local rules. Have site custodians review.

recap.question: Which city is the capital of Oriental Mindoro?
recap.onIncorrect: Explain the linked discovery and allow retry. Keep run rewards.
recap.reward: Optional journal reflection badge; never gate core travel progress.

journal.title: The city beyond arrival
journal.text: A provincial center can also be a place to learn and conserve. Link the museum stop with coastal habitat observation rather than treating Calapan only as a gateway.
journal.note: Draft editorial synthesis; factual basis is in linked discovery records.

introduction.text: Naujan's adventure can connect wetland life with built heritage at Bancuro. Naujan Lake is part of a wider landscape shared by several municipalities, rather than the story of one town alone.

collectibles.name: Fish observation card
collectibles.designNotes: Replace live-fish catching with identification; exact species require verified artwork.

collectibles.name: Bancuro heritage sketch
collectibles.designNotes: A drawing token, never a stone removed from ruins.

discoveries.title: International wetland
discoveries.text: Naujan Lake National Park entered the Ramsar list on 12 November 1999.

discoveries.title: Shared landscape
discoveries.text: The lake park profile describes a landscape surrounded by Naujan, Pola, Socorro and Victoria.

discoveries.title: Fishery knowledge
discoveries.text: A 2025â€“2026 assessment studied Lake Naujan's fisheries to inform sustainable management.

discoveries.title: Bancuro heritage
discoveries.text: The town history describes Bancuro's stone church as a place of worship and refuge.

discoveries.title: A name story
discoveries.text: The tourism history presents a thirst-related origin of Naujan's name as a legend.

visitorChallenge.text: Observe birds from a distance and keep litter out of the lake. Enjoy historic places without removing stones or objects.
visitorChallenge.note: Proposed respectful-behavior mechanic; not quoted local rules. Have site custodians review.

recap.question: Naujan Lake National Park is recognized internationally as what?
recap.onIncorrect: Explain the linked discovery and allow retry. Keep run rewards.
recap.reward: Optional journal reflection badge; never gate core travel progress.

journal.title: Water holds shared stories
journal.text: Lake research, surrounding communities and Bancuro's heritage belong to different parts of Naujan's story. Protecting water and respecting historic places can be learned together.
journal.note: Draft editorial synthesis; factual basis is in linked discovery records.

introduction.text: Victoria combines rice fields with varied fruit harvests. Explore its fruit-basket identity, discover crops such as rambutan and lanzones, and follow the connection between farming, processing and everyday livelihoods.

collectibles.name: Rambutan and lanzones basket
collectibles.designNotes: Replace unrelated fruit mix with documented crops.

collectibles.name: Calamansi juice parcel
collectibles.designNotes: Connect farming to value-added local processing.

discoveries.title: Fruit-basket identity
discoveries.text: A UP food-systems study describes Victoria as Oriental Mindoro's fruit basket.

discoveries.title: Rice matters too
discoveries.text: The same study emphasizes rice alongside the town's fruit production.

discoveries.title: Orchard variety
discoveries.text: Its documented crops include calamansi, bananas, lanzones, mangosteen and rambutan.

discoveries.title: Processing livelihoods
discoveries.text: A provincial report describes a Victoria enterprise processing calamansi into juice and concentrate.

discoveries.title: Agricultural learning
discoveries.text: DA's station profile places an agricultural research station in Alcate, Victoria.

visitorChallenge.text: Value the work behind every harvest. Choose produce thoughtfully, avoid food waste and keep market spaces clean.
visitorChallenge.note: Proposed respectful-behavior mechanic; not quoted local rules. Have site custodians review.

recap.question: Which combination better reflects Victoria's documented farming identity?
recap.onIncorrect: Explain the linked discovery and allow retry. Keep run rewards.
recap.reward: Optional journal reflection badge; never gate core travel progress.

journal.title: From harvest to livelihood
journal.text: Victoria's story can move from field and orchard to market and processing. The collectible basket represents farm work and variety, not a claim that every fruit grows only here.
journal.note: Draft editorial synthesis; factual basis is in linked discovery records.

introduction.text: Socorro is an agricultural municipality connected to the southern side of Naujan Lake. Its local identity combines farming, freshwater livelihoods and a documented history of separation from Pola.

collectibles.name: Calamansi harvest crate
collectibles.designNotes: Documented crop; replace a generic live-fish pickup if the mission focuses on farming.

collectibles.name: Lake observation badge
collectibles.designNotes: A shared-wetland token, not a private municipal emblem.

discoveries.title: Created from Pola
discoveries.text: Republic Act 3609 separated Socorro's territory from Pola.

discoveries.title: Creation date checked
discoveries.text: The original law was approved on 22 June 1963.

discoveries.title: Earlier settlement name
discoveries.text: The municipal website links the town's history to Catiningan.

discoveries.title: Agricultural variety
discoveries.text: PPDO's municipal history lists calamansi, rambutan, coffee and bananas among Socorro's crops.

discoveries.title: Lake connection
discoveries.text: The conservation profile includes Socorro among the four municipalities surrounding Naujan Lake National Park.

visitorChallenge.text: Care for the water connecting farms and the lake. Keep packaging and other waste out of waterways.
visitorChallenge.note: Proposed respectful-behavior mechanic; not quoted local rules. Have site custodians review.

recap.question: Socorro was separated from which municipality?
recap.onIncorrect: Explain the linked discovery and allow retry. Keep run rewards.
recap.reward: Optional journal reflection badge; never gate core travel progress.

journal.title: Farm and freshwater crossroads
journal.text: Socorro's fields and lake connection create a story about livelihoods linked by water. Its foundation date comes from the original law, not a conflicting historical summary.
journal.note: Draft editorial synthesis; factual basis is in linked discovery records.

introduction.text: Pola connects an estuary and coastal setting with a concentration of ancestral houses. Its recorded livelihoods include farming, fishing and nipa weaving, offering both built-heritage and everyday-work stories.

collectibles.name: Nipa-woven panel token
collectibles.designNotes: Design requires a local maker's review; represent work, not harvesting wild plants.

collectibles.name: Heritage-window postcard
collectibles.designNotes: Original illustration, not a removable architectural fragment.

discoveries.title: Ancestral houses
discoveries.text: The tourism portal describes Pola's concentration of preserved ancestral houses.

discoveries.title: River and town
discoveries.text: The town history places the poblacion at the Casiligan River's estuary.

discoveries.title: Everyday livelihoods
discoveries.text: Its historical account identifies agriculture and fishing among local livelihoods.

discoveries.title: Nipa craft
discoveries.text: The same account explicitly mentions nipa weaving.

discoveries.title: Red-clay account
discoveries.text: The history links Pola's name with reddish clay and the word pula.

visitorChallenge.text: Remember that heritage houses may be lived-in homes. Ask before entering or photographing residents.

introduction.text: Mansalay brings a coastal landscape into conversation with Hanunoo Mangyan literary heritage. NCCA connects the poet Ginaw Bilog with Mansalay and the ambahan tradition, offering a specific cultural starting point.

collectibles.designNotes: A journal unlock rather than a sacred object or copied poem.

collectibles.name: Beach observation postcard
collectibles.designNotes: Replace shell-taking with a drawn memory.

discoveries.title: A named culture bearer

discoveries.title: Everyday themes
